title: Tiffani Faison to close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool’s Errand in the Fenway
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Tiffani Faison will close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool’s Errand in Fenway in November when their lease ends.
Faison cites rising costs and an unsustainable business environment as main reasons for the restaurant closures.
Sweet Cheeks Q, a celebrated barbecue restaurant, will end its 15-year run, impacting 45 staff members.

title: Take a look inside New Hampshire’s oldest continuously operated inn after a makeover
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Inn at Hancock in New Hampshire, established in 1789, reopened in May after a three-year renovation.
Renovations were led by co-owner Kerri Landry and Boston-based designer Jeffrey Delvy, blending history with modern luxury.
The inn offers three suite types with amenities like free Wi-Fi, fireplaces, and luxury bath products; rates start at $620.

title: Acton teen accused of killing mom, brother ordered held without bail
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, accused of killing mother Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and brother Siddharth, 14, held without bail.
Prosecutors found signs of violent struggle in Acton home; victims died from blunt force trauma.
Aravind charged with multiple counts, including murder, and will undergo mental health evaluation.

title: Downtown Boston was buzzing in July. Here’s a look at the numbers.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Downtown Boston saw a 10.5% increase in domestic foot traffic in July 2026 compared to July 2025.
Weekend foot traffic in downtown Boston returned to 104% of 2019 levels, according to Downtown Boston Alliance data.
Temple Place in Downtown Crossing experienced a 40% sales boost for 11 businesses during World Cup events.

title: 2 seriously injured in West End stabbing, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two people were seriously injured in a stabbing incident Thursday morning in Boston's West End.
The man suffered self-inflicted, life-threatening injuries, while the woman's injuries were not life-threatening.
Police believe the incident was domestic in nature and are investigating; tips can be sent to the Boston Police Homicide Unit.

title: Healey temporarily restricts kratom sales statewide
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey has temporarily designated all kratom forms as Schedule I substances in Massachusetts to prevent abuse.
The restriction gives local officials authority to enforce actions against retailers selling kratom, effective after a 14-day notice.
Kratom's varying potency and lack of oversight pose public health risks, sparking state-led educational initiatives and regulations.

title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, Cape Cod, is highlighted as New England's top beach town, featuring beaches, oyster specials, and sunset cruises.
Ogunquit, Maine, named best New England beach town, offers scenic day trips and numerous activities for visitors this season.
Chach Restaurant in Provincetown will permanently close on November 3 after 21 years, prompting community support.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident off Cape Cod near Sesuit Harbor on Wednesday around 5 p.m.
The search involved marine units from Dennis, Barnstable, and Sandwich, plus aerial support from the U.S. Coast Guard.
The diver was found around 5:30 p.m. and pronounced dead at Sesuit Harbor; the incident is under investigation.

title: Lindsay Clancy’s raw journal entries read in court
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Prosecutors requested access to logs of Lindsay Clancy's courthouse visitors during her trial, including a forensic psychologist and a priest.
Lead investigator Trooper Joshua McKelligan testified about crime scene findings and Clancy's medications discovered in her home.
Clancy's cellphone data revealed journaling on parenting struggles and Google searches days before her children's deaths.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: Westerly, Rhode Island beach house built in 1987 features 2,724 sq ft, 3 bedrooms, and 3 baths.
The property offers contemporary cottage style with water views on both sides; 2025 taxes are $11,125.
The listing price for the beach house is one of three options: $1.98 million, $1.88 million, or $1.78 million.
